question: If $F(x)$ is an anti-derivative of $f(x)$, show that $\frac{d}{dx}\int f(x)dx=f(x)$.
explanation:
Let $F(x)$ be an anti-derivative of $f(x)$ so $F'(x)=f(x)$.

By definition $\int f(x)dx = F(x)+C$.

Differentiating gives $\frac{d}{dx}[F(x)+C]=F'(x)$.

Thus $\frac{d}{dx}\int f(x)dx=f(x)$.
